questions.problem: Let $C=\{-3,-1,1,3\}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${1}_{C}(-1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The indicator function $1[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false.

$$
1[P]=\{\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }P\text{ is true}, \\ 0, & \text{if }P\text{ is false}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the indicator function ${1}_{C}(x)$ of a set $C$ equals $1$ if $x\in C$ and $0$ if $x\notin C.$ This can be written using Iverson bracket notation as

$$
{1}_{C}(x)=1[x\in C].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{1}_{C}(-1)=1[-1\in C]=1[-1\in \{-3,-1,1,3\}].
$$

The expression $1[{x}_{i}>0]\cdot {x}_{i}$ equals ${x}_{i}$ when ${x}_{i}>0$ and equals $0$ otherwise. Thus, the sum 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}1[{x}_{i}>0]\cdot {x}_{i}
$$

adds up only the positive values.

We evaluate the indicator function for each ${x}_{i}:$

- $1[{x}_{1}>0]=1[9>0]=1$

- $1[{x}_{2}>0]=1[-8>0]=0$

- $1[{x}_{3}>0]=1[-1>0]=0$

- $1[{x}_{4}>0]=1[4>0]=1$

- $1[{x}_{5}>0]=1[2>0]=1$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}1[{x}_{i}>0]\cdot {x}_{i} & =1\cdot 9+0\cdot (-8)+0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 4+1\cdot 2 \\  & =9+0+0+4+2 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
1[P]=\{\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }P\text{ is true}, \\ 0, & \text{if }P\text{ is false}.\end{aligned}
$$

The expression $1[{x}_{i}\ge 0]\cdot (2{x}_{i})+1[{x}_{i}<0]\cdot 1$ equals $2{x}_{i}$ when ${x}_{i}\ge 0$ and equals $1$ when ${x}_{i}<0.$ Thus, the sum

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}1[{x}_{i}\ge 0]\cdot (2{x}_{i})+1[{x}_{i}<0]\cdot 1
$$

adds $2{x}_{i}$ for nonnegative values and $1$ for negative values.

We evaluate the indicator function for each ${x}_{i}:$

- $1[{x}_{1}\ge 0]=1[-6\ge 0]=0,$ $1[{x}_{1}<0]=1$

- $1[{x}_{2}\ge 0]=1[-1\ge 0]=0,$ $1[{x}_{2}<0]=1$

- $1[{x}_{3}\ge 0]=1[0\ge 0]=1,$ $1[{x}_{3}<0]=0$

- $1[{x}_{4}\ge 0]=1[4\ge 0]=1,$ $1[{x}_{4}<0]=0$

- $1[{x}_{5}\ge 0]=1[7\ge 0]=1,$ $1[{x}_{5}<0]=0$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}1[{x}_{i}\ge 0]\cdot (2{x}_{i})+1[{x}_{i}<0]\cdot 1 & =1+1+2\cdot 0+2\cdot 4+2\cdot 7 \\  & =1+1+0+8+14 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $B=\{2,4,6,8\}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to $1[5\in B]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The indicator function $1[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false.

$$
1[P]=\{\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }P\text{ is true}, \\ 0, & \text{if }P\text{ is false}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the indicator function ${1}_{A}(x)$ of a set $A$ equals $1$ if $x\in A$ and $0$ if $x\notin A.$ This can be written using Iverson bracket notation as

$$
{1}_{A}(x)=1[x\in A].
$$

Here, the Iverson bracket expression $1[5\in B]$ has $x=5$ and $A=B.$ Therefore, converting back to set indicator notation, we have

$$
1[5\in B]={1}_{B}(5).
$$
